question.worked_solution:
To calculate the limit, we multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the denominator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,2}h(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \,2}\frac{x-2}{\sqrt{x+a}-\sqrt{2+a}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \,2}(\frac{x-2}{\sqrt{x+a}-\sqrt{2+a}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{x+a}+\sqrt{2+a}}{\sqrt{x+a}+\sqrt{2+a}}) \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \,2}\frac{(x-2)(\sqrt{x+a}+\sqrt{2+a})}{(\sqrt{x+a})^{2}-(\sqrt{2+a})^{2}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \,2}\frac{(x-2)(\sqrt{x+a}+\sqrt{2+a})}{x-2} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \,2}\frac{\cancel{(x-2)}(\sqrt{x+a}+\sqrt{2+a})}{\cancel{x-2}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \,2}(\sqrt{x+a}+\sqrt{2+a}) \\  & =2\sqrt{2+a}.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $h(x)$ to be continuous at $x=2,$ we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,2}h(x) & =h(2) \\ 2\sqrt{2+a} & =6 \\ \sqrt{2+a} & =3 \\ 2+a & =9 \\ a & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, setting $a=7$ removes the point discontinuity.
